name: Clinical Trial Site Lookup
description: Helps clinical trial site selectors find active research sites by therapeutic area, phase, and geography. Searches ClinicalTrials.gov + your internal CRO database, ranks by enrollment performance and capacity, returns enriched output with PI, site status, and recent enrollment trend. Read-only — no PHI write paths.
outcomes: 30–50% reduction in site-identification cycle time per trial by automating ClinicalTrials.gov + internal CRO database queries
5–10 hours/week saved per site selector on manual database lookups
Auditable answer trail with cited sources for every site recommendation
Faster trial start-up — each day of earlier start-up avoids ~$40K/day in direct phase-3 trial cost (and far more in at-risk peak revenue)

roi.savings: $150K–400K/year (illustrative) in site-selector time — excludes the much larger avoided trial-delay cost (~$40K/day of earlier start-up)
roi.cost: $15K–40K/year — Bedrock (Claude Sonnet) + Knowledge Base (OpenSearch Serverless ~$350/mo floor) + AgentCore Gateway + CloudWatch
roi.multiple: ~5–20x on selector time alone; materially higher once trial-delay avoidance is counted
roi.assumes: Illustrative: mid-size CRO/sponsor running 30+ active trials; site selectors at ~$110/hr loaded; phase-3 delay costs ~$40K/day in direct trial spend (NIH). Validate with your own numbers.

idealCustomer.size: Mid-market pharma sponsors, CROs (Contract Research Organizations), academic medical centers running multi-site trials
idealCustomer.volume: 30+ active trials at any time; site-selection touches 50–500 candidate sites per trial
idealCustomer.team: 1–5 site selectors per therapeutic area; supported by feasibility analysts
triggers: Trials repeatedly missing first-patient-in milestones due to site activation delays
Site selectors spending hours per day in ClinicalTrials.gov + internal CRO portals
No structured way to compare candidate sites by recent enrollment performance
Leadership asking 'why is site identification so slow?'
disqualifiers: Single-site or investigator-initiated trials (no selection problem to solve)
You have no internal CRO database to enrich the public data with
Heavily regulated trials where site selection is contractually fixed upstream

customerCustomizes: Internal CRO database connection (BigQuery / Postgres / Snowflake / proprietary CTMS)
Therapeutic-area taxonomy and synonyms specific to the sponsor
Site-ranking weights (enrollment speed vs. capacity vs. PI track record)
preBuilt: AgentCore Managed Harness with the trial-site-lookup system prompt
Knowledge Base structure for therapeutic-area docs + site profiles
Guardrails template (refuse PHI inputs, no diagnostic claims, citation requirement)
CloudWatch dashboard (queries/day, citation rate, source mix, latency)
AGENTS.md + build-spec/ contract for a coding agent to implement
sharedResponsibility: Read-only kit. You own deployed harness config, KB content, and the connection to your CRO database. AWS does not handle PHI in this kit; the agent refuses inputs containing PHI patterns and the data sources are non-PHI by design.
